Butler-Portugal canonical representative of a double coset

Source: R/tensor-can.R
double_coset_can_rep.Rd

Port of SymPy's double_coset_can_rep(), the Butler-Portugal algorithm for tensor canonicalization with dummy indices. The tensor is the permutation g (size n + 2, the last two points carry the sign); the slot symmetry group S has minimal BSGS b_S, sgens; the dummy symmetry group D is built from dummies and sym. The result is the minimum of D*g*S under lexicographic order, or 0 when the tensor vanishes.

Usage

double_coset_can_rep(dummies, sym, b_S, sgens, S_transversals, g)

Arguments

dummies

List of integer vectors of dummy indices, one per index type, ordered d0, -d0, d1, -d1, ....

sym

List of metric symmetries, one per index type: NULL, 0 or 1.

b_S

Base of a minimal slot symmetry BSGS.

sgens

Strong generators of the slot symmetry (permutations).

S_transversals

Transversals of the slot BSGS, from get_transversals().

g

The permutation representing the tensor.

Value

An integer vector (array form), or 0.

Examples

gens <- list(Permutation(c(2, 1, 0, 3, 4, 5, 7, 6)), Permutation(c(4, 1, 2, 3, 0, 5, 7, 6)))
base <- c(0, 2)
tr <- get_transversals(base, gens)
double_coset_can_rep(list(0:5), list(0), base, gens, tr, Permutation(c(4, 2, 0, 1, 3, 5, 6, 7)))
#> [1] 0 1 2 3 4 5 7 6
double_coset_can_rep(list(0:5), list(0), base, gens, tr, Permutation(c(4, 1, 3, 0, 5, 2, 6, 7)))
#> [1] 0
